answer: Natural-language hypothesis (final): Both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) were characterized by a NEGATIVE first principal component (PC1) of the PCA on the forms of capital in hundred-year slices — i.e., a capital composite below its long-run average. The Middle Neolithic was the deeper negative: mean PC1 ≈ −1.39 ± 0.50 (≈0.72 sd below the 39-slice mean of 0; all 5 slices negative, from −0.59 at 3400 BCE to −1.81 at 3000 BCE). The Younger Neolithic was a slightly shallower negative plateau: mean PC1 ≈ −1.13 ± 0.44 (≈0.59 sd below baseline; all 7 slices negative, from −0.42 at 2300 BCE to −1.62 at 2800 BCE). Both phases fall between the strongly negative Early Neolithic (−1.76 ± 0.44) and the positive Late Neolithic (+0.33 ± 0.86): PC1 rises steadily across the Neolithic but does not cross from negative to positive until after ~2100 BCE. The two phases differ in which forms of capital drive the negative PC1 (sign convention: sum of PC1 loadings fixed > 0, so positive loadings = wealth/prestige capital, negative = mixed). The Middle Neolithic negative PC1 is driven mainly by suppressed social capital (Monument Count, Copper&Gold) and cultural/pottery forms (contributions −0.49 and −0.47), with symbolic capital (houses, hatchets/swords, daggers) already near baseline (−0.11). The Younger Neolithic negative PC1 is driven mainly by suppressed economic capital (Depot, Sickle, Axes&Celt, Monument Size; −0.47) and cultural/pottery forms (−0.43), while social capital has swung back to roughly neutral (+0.00).

payload.workflow: 1) Load data/capital.csv (39 hundred-year BCE slices 4300..500); convert comma decimals to floats; drop group/color metadata; confirm 12 Z variables complete (0 NAs) and identical to time_series raw values. 2) Correlation-based PCA: standardize the 12 Z variables across the 39 slices (SVD); fix PC1 sign so sum of loadings > 0 (PC1 = capital composite); report loadings per variable and per capital type (symbolic/social/cultural/economic), eigenvalue (3.64, 30.3% variance) and per-slice PC1 scores. 3) Characterize Middle Neolithic (BCE 3400..3000, 5 slices) and Younger Neolithic (BCE 2900..2300, 7 slices): mean PC1 ± sd vs whole-series baseline (0) and vs EN (4300..3500) and LN (2200..1700); dominant capital types via sum of loading × standardized value per type per phase. 4) Pollen Belau_PC1 kept separate as optional demographic/openness context, clearly labeled. 5) Final candidate = natural-language hypothesis above.
